niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Great question — “shadow work” and spiritual practice can mean different things depending on whether you want psychological integration, trauma-healing, meditation/embodied practice, or a mix of Jungian and transpersonal approaches. Below I’ve organized a practical, vetted list of online courses/platforms (free and paid), plus safety notes and a suggested learning path so you can pick what fits you best.

Top course/platform recommendations (by focus)

1) Foundations: mindfulness and stable practice (recommended first)
- Palouse Mindfulness (free MBSR course): a faithful online version of Jon Kabat‑Zinn’s 8‑week MBSR curriculum. Good for building attention, distress tolerance, and body awareness before deeper inner work.
- 10% Happier (app & courses): practical, secular meditation courses and teachers; good for steady daily practice.
- Waking Up (Sam Harris app): practical meditation + theory for students who prefer secular/non-dual viewpoints.

2) Trauma‑informed, parts‑work (recommended if you have difficult or traumatic material)
- IFS Institute — Introductory resources and workshops (Internal Family Systems): evidence-based and widely used for working with “parts” (shadow material) safely. If you have trauma or complex inner parts, IFS is a strong, compassionate option.
Note: IFS trainings are also offered by certified practitioners as group courses or therapy.

3) Jungian / “shadow” specific work
- The Jung Platform: a subscription platform offering courses and webinars on Jungian shadow work, archetypes, dreams, and myth — taught by Jungian analysts and authors. Good if your interest is archetypal, symbolic, psychoanalytic exploration.
- Sounds True / Shift Network (courses by established teachers): these platforms regularly host shadow-work programs (including archived courses by Debbie Ford, James Hollis, etc.). Quality varies by teacher; check instructor credentials.

4) Somatic & embodied integration
- Insight Timer (paid courses + free content): many teachers offer courses on somatic healing, embodiment, and integration practices; good if you want body‑based approaches.
- Somatic practices and trauma-informed breath/work — look for courses taught by credentialed somatic therapists. (Note: full Somatic Experiencing or Sensorimotor Psychotherapy trainings are professional-level.)

5) General spiritual/ethical foundations
- Teachers with strong meditation/compassion programs: Tara Brach, Jack Kornfield, Sharon Salzberg — each offers online retreats, multi‑week courses, or programs via their sites/Sounds True. Great for applying spiritual practice to emotional healing and shadow material.

6) Short/affordable introductions and marketplaces
- Udemy / Coursera / Skillshare: you’ll find many “shadow work” courses. Quality is variable — read reviews, instructor credentials, and sample videos before buying.
- Coursera: psychology and well‑being courses (e.g., Yale’s “The Science of Well‑Being”) are useful complements to shadow/spiritual work.

How to choose a course
- If you have a history of trauma, severe depression, or suicidal thoughts: prioritize trauma‑informed programs and work with a licensed therapist. Avoid solo deep dives into shadow work without support.
- If you want experiential meditation skills first: choose MBSR/10% Happier/Waking Up or a teacher like Tara Brach/Kornfield.
- If you want archetypal exploration (dreams, myth, Jung): choose Jung Platform and Jungian teachers/authors.
- If you want parts-based integration: choose IFS resources or a certified IFS practitioner.

Safety & ethical considerations
- Shadow work can surface strong emotions, memories, and impulses. Have a support plan (therapist, trusted friend, grounding practices).
- Prefer teachers who are trauma‑informed and transparent about contraindications.
- Look for courses that include integration time, peer support or live Q&A, and clear boundaries for working with intense material.

Practical next steps
- If you’re new: start with Palouse Mindfulness or a beginner meditation course for 6–8 weeks.
- If you’re ready for inner‑work after stable practice: try an introductory IFS course or a Jungian course on The Jung Platform.
- If you want structured shadow work with guided exercises: look for offerings on Sounds True or Shift Network taught by experienced clinicians.

Recommended books to pair with courses
- Owning Your Own Shadow — Robert A. Johnson
- The Dark Side of the Light Chasers — Debbie Ford
- No Bad Parts — Richard Schwartz (on IFS)
- The Body Keeps the Score — Bessel van der Kolk (trauma context)

Would you like a tailored short list?
If you tell me:
- whether you have trauma or major mental‑health concerns,
- which spiritual tradition or style you prefer (Buddhist, Jungian, secular mindfulness, shamanic, etc.), and
- whether you want free vs paid courses,
I’ll recommend 3–5 specific courses and show expected time commitments and price ranges.
